items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: We were in Los Angeles here playing at some club, and we had Sunday we had off. So Ray and I, we roomed together and we’d play golf.

ctx.x: With this trio, tell us some of the maybe more humorous things that happened in the trio.

Oh. All right. We were in Los Angeles here playing at some club, and we had Sunday we had off. So Ray and I, we roomed together and we’d play golf. And it was late in the afternoon so we had this idea. Well coming home from golf, and I saw this advertisement in a drug store, and it said, “Dye your hair any color” and then it would wash right out any time you wash your hair. So I had an idea, and Ray went for it but he was kind of leery about it. See I had bright red hair at the time, and Ray’s was jet black. So…
How much is humor a part of the very fabric of jazz?

items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I think certainly playing with Oscar and Ray was a highlight.

ctx.x: You’ve played with so many of the great, great people in jazz, and so many have played with you. Is there, in your career, what are the highlights for you? Have we already mentioned them?

Hmmm. Highlights. I think certainly playing with Oscar and Ray was a highlight. And then playing with all the other people in Jazz at the Philharmonic. And what was a great reward for me and great confidence builder, almost all the ones when they’d make their own records they’d use me.

items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: Herb Ellis on guitar; Oscar Peterson on piano; Ray Brown on bass

ctx.x: Yeah but that was the backlash of something that happened before. We were in Japan and we used to have something called a Ballad Medley. The Ballad Medley was everybody playing one chorus of whatever ballad he chose to play. So what they did is they would black out the stage, put a spotlight just in the front at the microphone. The first guy would walk out, he would walk past Oscar and he’d say “’I’ve Got It Bad’ B flat” and then he’d

walk over. As he’s walking to the mic Oscar would do a four or eight bar introduction. He’d play one chorus. And then as he’s walking off to applause, the next guy walked by and Oscar would say so-and-so-and-so. And that’s the Ballad Medley. Okay. Now all of these tricks and stuff are still going on. I used to lay my bass on the stage, because we’d have a break at intermission, and then we would start the second half with Ella Fitzgerald. So they would call Buddy Rich, Herb Ellis, Ray Brown, Oscar Peterson, and…
So Oscar started it and the whole thing came in a big circle.
